comparable.challenge: handle: 41-byte handle (genuine plus a trailing byte)
comparable.finding: the verifier reads only the first 40 bytes of `pk`; bytes beyond are ignored, so distinct handle encodings name one key: an adapter MUST enforce exactly 40 bytes before committing to keccak(handle)

comparable.challenge: handle: 72-byte handle (genuine plus 32 trailing bytes)
comparable.finding: the verifier reads only the first 40 bytes of `pk`; bytes beyond are ignored, so distinct handle encodings name one key: an adapter MUST enforce exactly 40 bytes before committing to keccak(handle)

comparable.challenge: blob: both halves deployed by a plain CREATE outside setKey, same bytes
comparable.finding: setKey adds nothing the verifier later checks: any address pair holding the right bytes is a key, so handle-to-key binding must come from a publisher the kernel can audit (PUBLISHER_BINDING.md)

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 31 (outer tuple: offset word of element 0, low byte (byte 31))
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 100 (outer tuple: length word of element 0, byte 100 (a framing word the reader never loads))
comparable.finding: this byte is never read: two blobs with different code hashes name the same key, so a blob's EXTCODEHASH is not a key identity and a publisher must bind the canonical public key, not the blob bytes

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 515 (aHat[0][0] word 0, byte 3: low byte of field 0 (a coefficient))
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 543 (aHat[0][0] word 0, byte 31: low byte of field 7 (a coefficient))
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 512 (aHat[0][0] word 0, byte 0: the padding bits above a 23-bit coefficient in a 32-bit field)
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 16746 (tr, byte 10)
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 17055 (t1[0] word 0, byte 31: low byte of a coefficient)
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: blob: one bit flipped at half-0 byte 17024 (t1[0] word 0, byte 0: padding bits)
comparable.finding: a corrupted expansion is read as a different key with no integrity error: a wrong blob is silently a wrong key

comparable.challenge: degenerate key (degenerate rho A): pk = rho || 0^1920, sigma = c~ || zEncode(0) || 0^61
comparable.finding: ML-DSA offers no exclusive ownership: a FIPS-conformant verifier accepts a key-free forgery for a degenerate key. The kernel cannot see t1; a registration gate must refuse pk[32..1952) == 0 (and the client must derive keys from a seed). Subtler degenerate classes are UNKNOWN here.

comparable.challenge: degenerate key (degenerate rho B): pk = rho || 0^1920, sigma = c~ || zEncode(0) || 0^61
comparable.finding: ML-DSA offers no exclusive ownership: a FIPS-conformant verifier accepts a key-free forgery for a degenerate key. The kernel cannot see t1; a registration gate must refuse pk[32..1952) == 0 (and the client must derive keys from a seed). Subtler degenerate classes are UNKNOWN here.

comparable.challenge: signature: empty signature
comparable.finding: length is checked first: 0xFFFFFFFF on the ERC-7913 path, InvalidSignatureLength on the context path, both before any key read

comparable.challenge: signature: 3,308 bytes
comparable.finding: length is checked first: 0xFFFFFFFF on the ERC-7913 path, InvalidSignatureLength on the context path, both before any key read

comparable.challenge: signature: 3,310 bytes
comparable.finding: length is checked first: 0xFFFFFFFF on the ERC-7913 path, InvalidSignatureLength on the context path, both before any key read

comparable.challenge: signature: 4,096 bytes
comparable.finding: length is checked first: 0xFFFFFFFF on the ERC-7913 path, InvalidSignatureLength on the context path, both before any key read

comparable.challenge: signature: 3,309 zero bytes
comparable.finding: a constant signature is rejected by the decoder or the final hash

comparable.challenge: signature: 3,309 bytes of 0xff
comparable.finding: a constant signature is rejected by the decoder or the final hash

comparable.challenge: public key: lengths 0, 32, 1951, 1953, 40320 at expansion
comparable.finding: the verifier never sees a canonical public key; its only key input is the 40-byte handle, so canonical-key validation is entirely off-chain or in a publisher

comparable.challenge: helper: code at the bound address replaced by other code
comparable.finding: EXTCODEHASH binding holds: a helper with any other code is refused on every call, so the residual risk is the PROVENANCE of the pinned bytes themselves, not substitution

comparable.challenge: sponge: 50 raw permutations and 37 batched SHAKE256 messages vs @noble/hashes
comparable.finding: behavioural agreement with an independent implementation on these inputs; NOT a proof, and no substitute for the lost generator of f1600_core.hex

comparable.challenge: routing: |M| = 733, empty context (mu preimage 799 bytes)
comparable.finding: batched path

comparable.challenge: routing: |M| = 734, empty context (mu preimage 800 bytes)
comparable.finding: the 800-byte preimage takes shake256Fast (raw permutation protocol) because the batched helper entry cannot express it; verdict unchanged

comparable.challenge: routing: |M| = 735, empty context (mu preimage 801 bytes)
comparable.finding: batched path
